findings.title: Rebuild re-runs the issue freeze before the reuse check, so a qualified case can change or get a second record
findings.description:
The data flow puts discovery and the issue freeze (steps 1–2) before the reuse check (step 4). Line 241 says the reuse check needs the post-install environment digest. So every `build` fetches every issue again and re-renders it.

If an issue body was edited after a case qualified, the next build rejects that commit with `issue_edited_after_fix` under a `…-pre` record id. The earlier `…-<env>` qualified record stays. The commit then has two records with opposite outcomes. This breaks three things:
- Line 142 says "the case is never fetched again".
- The architecture says "Issue text is frozen into the case when it is created".
- Line 373 says "the number of records equals the number of closing commits".

The record-count rule also fails in a second way. The record id includes the environment digest (line 240), so a new interpreter or uv version adds a second record for the same commit.

**Fix:**
- Check for an existing qualified record or case for the commit before fetching the issue again, and reuse its `task_text`.
- State which record `yield_report` and `fix-cases show` use when a commit has records under several environments, or under `pre` and an environment. For example: the latest by `created_at`, or only the current environment.
- Restate the record-count rule as "per environment".

findings.title: What a timed-out suite run produces is ambiguous, and its nodes can be misread as test verdicts
findings.description:
421 D10 says a timeout does not raise. It returns `SuiteRun(timed_out=True)` and marks every node without a result `not_run`.

D5 maps `not_run` to `undecidable_failure_at_parent`, which is a test rejection. It also says "A timeout … records `harness_error`". The doc does not say which rule wins, so an implementation that maps per node will charge a harness timeout to the case.

The same gap affects D9's repeats (lines 222–226). If one of the three reference runs times out, its nodes are `not_run`, they "differ across runs", and they get rejected or excluded as `flaky`. That also changes the case id.

**Fix:** State that `SuiteRun.timed_out` is checked first, in both D5 and D9, and turns the whole candidate into `harness_error` before any per-node mapping. Add a test with a fixture timeout during the repeats.

findings.title: Failure handling for the trace, collect, resolver and `gh` paths is contradictory or missing
Wrapping `_patch.__enter__`/`start` does not catch `patch.dict`, so a test that patches project code can qualify
findings.description:
D7 says wrapping `unittest.mock._patch.__enter__` / `start` "covers `patch`, `patch.object` and `patch.dict`". It does not. In `unittest.mock`, `patch.dict` is the separate class `_patch_dict`, with its own `__enter__`, `start` and decorator path.

As written, `patch.dict("pkg.mod.REGISTRY", …)` on a project module's dict would not be intercepted. The test would pass D7 and be admitted. The architecture says a check that cannot decide must exclude ("never admitted"), and the slice plan's success criteria include a patched-internal test that fails the check.

**Fix:**
- Wrap `_patch_dict.__enter__` / `start` as well, and resolve its `in_dict` owner. When the target is a string, resolve it to the module that owns the dict.
- Add a `patch.dict` case to the trace plugin's fixture tests (line 388 already promises "each patch API").

findings.title: Hidden fixtures can depend on added conftest imports that the case never records for 425
D5 mixes `NodeOutcome` and `FailureKind` values under "FailureKind"
findings.description: `passed`, `skipped`, `xfailed`, `xpassed`, `not_run` and `error` are 421's `NodeOutcome` values. `FailureKind` is set only for `failed`/`error` (421 D11). The mapping should say it switches on `outcome` first, then on `failure_kind`. "`error` in setup or teardown" should also name its `phase` source. This is wording only; the intent is clear.

findings.title: "Used unchanged" overstates it; this slice extends `registry.py` and `MetrologyRecord`
findings.description: The slice adds a `FixCaseAdapter` mapping to 421's `registry.py` (line 98) and a `fix_qualification` payload to `MetrologyRecord` (line 352). Both are extension points that 421 anticipated (421 D3, D9), so the dependency direction is correct. 421 D9 expected 422 to add fairness methods to the adapter seam. Using a separate `FixCaseAdapter` protocol instead is a justified ISP choice and is stated at line 284. Rewording line 395 to "extends only the registry and record envelope; no change to sandbox, store primitives or suite runner" would avoid a false "421 defect" reading.

findings.title: Walkthrough step 6 expects case-set data from `yield --json`, which D12 does not define
findings.description: D12 says the yield report aggregates `FixQualification` records. It does not mention case sets. Either add the case set name and version to the yield JSON, or have step 6 check the set some other way.

findings.title: Fairness rule and test-set design match the architecture's principles
findings.description:
- **Test-first (D5):** maps 421's classification onto the arch's three-part rule.
- **Packaging boundary (D6):** uses the boundary as it stood at the parent, through `[project.scripts]` and top-level `__all__`. It rejects static-only checks and perturbation, consistent with the architecture.
- **No project patching (D7):** enforced, apart from the `patch.dict` gap above.
- **Test sets (D3):** node-level hidden and superseded sets, including added conftest fixtures.
- **Undecidable results** always exclude with a named reason.
- **Repeats (D9):** run at both the reference and the parent, and exclusions feed the case id, as the slice plan requires.

findings.title: Scope, dependencies and proportionality fit the slice plan entry
findings.description:
- Every success criterion in the slice plan entry is covered.
- Injection (425), replay and the leak scan (424), and slice cases (426) are excluded.
- The yield report's analytic bound is labelled as a stand-in, and its assumptions are spelled out (D12).
- A cross-project pool command is explicitly deferred (D13).
- `/sq:benchmark` is in scope because 421 deferred it to this slice.
- No new dependencies and no per-project configuration.
- The architecture states no latency or throughput NFR for this path, and this slice makes no LLM dispatch, so the cost-cap rules do not apply here.
